subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define execution anti-drift guards as a core durable run-state contract, and what artifact, timer, persistence, feature-flag, and escalation semantics should that contract enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but implementing it chooses core runtime semantics, durable state ownership, operator-visible escalation behavior, and new configuration or feature-flag shape.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Lifecycle Diagnostics
options.body: Treat these acceptance criteria as part of broader lifecycle and diagnostic recovery work so OpenClaw keeps one progress-state source of truth.

options.title: Keep Adjacent Safeguards Only
options.body: Decide current loop, liveness, and no-fake-progress mitigations are sufficient and narrow or close this issue after an explicit product call.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans core runtime state, product semantics, and ownership policy, and steipete is the strongest available code-owner signal from CODEOWNERS and current central-file history.
